hypothesis: DeepSeek V4's chain prompt matmuls on the per-row GEMV (chosen so a row's bits never depend on the chunking) leave the tiled GEMM idle on devices without cooperative matrices; letting prompt rows take the backend's tiled GEMM shortens the first token (the samples are prefill tok/s: prompt tokens over the time to the first token) without touching decode or a verify's bits.
model: DeepSeek V4 Flash (284B MoE), official FP4/FP8 checkpoint, 48 safetensors shards
command: docs/experiments/gemm-rows-2026-10-20/build-vk.sh && docs/experiments/gemm-rows-2026-10-20/campaign.sh  (c/deepseek_v4 MODEL --prompt-file docs/experiments/gemm-rows-2026-10-20/../prompt_2k.txt --max-tokens 32 --memory-gb 28; OMP_NUM_THREADS=16, COLI_TEMP=0, KVSAVE=0, V4_PREFIX_CKPT=0, COLI_VK_TIER_HOST=0; three interleaved runs per arm)

hardware.cpu: 24-thread x86-64 desktop CPU (8 performance + 8 efficiency cores)
hardware.storage: NVMe (model drive, ext4), expert shards read O_DIRECT
hardware.os: Arch Linux, gcc 15, Mesa RADV, Vulkan 1.4

quality.method: tests/test_vk_chain.c's gemv-rows section drives vkc_gemm_rows directly for both values on this device; the chain's exactness suite (make vk-chain-check) is green with the knob at 0 and at -1. Greedy text is not compared across arms: the GEMM is the documented row-canonical class, so texts may differ (they do).

evidence.uri: docs/experiments/gemm-rows-2026-10-20/ (six *-raw.txt run logs, samples.txt, sha256sums.txt; the manifest hash covers the six raw logs in name order)
